title: RPG Maker MZ question: how to 'upgrade' a town

posts.author: FateStCloud
posts.body:
Hey there,
working on an idea and was wondering if there is a way natively within MZ to essentially have a town upgrade function. Basically start with small town with multiple open plots of land > pay person to build a library > trigger cutscene > library on map is seen and shown, can be walked into etc.
Basically the issue I seem to be running into is getting the building to appear on the map as the building tiles are not attached to event panels and I am sure even if they were they would not link seamlessly (unless I am wrong on that?).
I figured I could just make a second copy of the map with the library built and swap maps that way however that means there is going to be like a million maps depending on if the player wants to build things in a different order.
If there is not a native way to handle this, is there is a plugin/script or anything that could assist with this?

posts.author: Aerosys
posts.body:
There's no native support, but with some creativity, you can achieve it.
An idea could be to use Events. Instead of building a house with many events (which would be super expensive), you can use a single event with a large sprite that just covers the whole house.
Alternatively, you could check out Shaz Tilechanger.
Tile Changer (Shaz's plugin for MV ported to MZ)
Shaz_TileChangerMZ.js by Shaz (original plugin) and SeaPhoenix (edits for MZ)  Prologue @Shaz has a great plugin to copy tiles and change tiles for MV, and I got their approval to port this plugin to MZ. The main edits are for compatibility, especially in terms of the plugin commands, and...

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
By default, maps are considered static - but as already said, there are ways around this.
However the beat way to do this depends on context or how many parts you want to change.
for a few tiles, all decorations (B to E tiles) can be used in events. for some cases you would have to copy ground tiles, but that only works as long as you have free space in the tileset.
a tile changer plugin has already been mentioned above. This works best with many but single changes.
for a lot of changes it would be easier to make a new map, especially if it is for multiple time changes. You would then have all transfers from and to the changing map have additional code checking a variable to decide to which map they actually transfer.
All of this does not yet consider event changes - for example if new buildings would require doors to enter them.
for a limited number of changes you can simply place the events as normal where the buildings are supposed to appear, and condition them to switches "building x build".
If there are many such events and the player can decide which building goes where, you might need to consider an event copy/clone plugin to dynamically create the required events.
that however will require a lot more coding to get the events working.
